## Genomic data {.custom1}

Package `vcfR` [@vcfr]

```{r echo=TRUE}
library(vcfR)
vcf = read.vcfR(file = "../Data/markers.vcf")
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno = extract.gt(x = vcf)
geno = geno[-grep(',', vcf@fix[,'ALT']),] # Remove multi-allelic mrks
vcf@fix = vcf@fix[-grep(',',vcf@fix[,'ALT']),]
geno = gsub('/', "", geno)
geno[1:5,1:5]
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
# Binding reference and alternative allele to marker matrix
geno = cbind(geno, vcf@fix[,c('REF', 'ALT')]) 
geno = apply(geno, 1, function(x){
  y = gsub('0', x['REF'], x)
  z = gsub('1', y['ALT'], y)
  z
})
geno[1:5,1:5]
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno = geno[-which(rownames(geno) %in% c('REF', 'ALT')), ]
geno[grep('CA', geno)] = 'AC'
geno[grep('GA', geno)] = 'AG'
geno[grep('TA', geno)] = 'AT'
geno[grep('GC', geno)] = 'CG'
geno[grep('TC', geno)] = 'CT'
geno[grep('TG', geno)] = 'GT'
geno[1:5,1:5]
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

**Filtering step**

```{r echo=TRUE}
Freqsnps = apply(geno, 2, table)
Freqsnps = do.call(rbind, lapply(Freqsnps, data.frame)) |> 
  rownames_to_column("mrk") |> mutate(mrk = gsub('\\..*', '', mrk))
head(Freqsnps)
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

**Filtering step**

```{r echo=TRUE}
Freqall = apply(geno, 2, function(x){
  aux = as.data.frame(table(do.call(c, strsplit(x = x, split = ''))))
  return(aux)
})
Freqall = do.call(rbind, Freqall) |> 
  rownames_to_column("mrk") |> mutate(mrk = gsub('\\..*', '', mrk))
head(Freqall)
Freqmis = apply(geno, 2, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))
head(Freqmis)
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

Removing markers with $\geq$ 5% of missing data

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno = geno[,-which(Freqmis >= 0.05)]  
vcf@fix = vcf@fix[-which(Freqmis >= 0.05),]  
dim(geno)
any(is.na(geno))
```

. . .

[Impute missing data with the mode]{.red}

```{r echo=TRUE}
for (i in colnames(geno)) {
  if(!any(is.na(geno[,i]))) next else{
    geno[which(is.na(geno[,i])),i] = as.character(
      Freqsnps[which(Freqsnps$mrk == i), ][which.max(Freqsnps[which(Freqsnps$mrk == i), ][,'Freq']), "Var1"]
      )
  }
  rm(i)
}
any(is.na(geno))
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

Removing markers with MAF $\leq$ 5%

```{r echo=TRUE}
Freqall$Fper = Freqall$Freq / (nrow(geno) * 2)
geno = geno[,-which(Freqall$Fper <= 0.05)]
dim(geno)
```

## Genomic data {.custom1}

**Re-codification according to the dosage of the reference allele**

```{r echo=TRUE}
geno.code = matrix(
  nrow = nrow(geno),
  ncol = ncol(geno),
  dimnames = list(rownames(geno), colnames(geno))
)
for (i in colnames(geno)) {
  x = geno[, i]
  geno.code[, i] = nchar(gsub(paste0("[^", vcf@fix[which(vcf@fix[, "ID"] == i),
                                                   'REF'], "]"), "", x))
}
geno.code[1:5,1:5]
# saveRDS(geno.code, file = "Data/mrk_filtered.RDS")
```

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

$$
\boldsymbol y = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol W \boldsymbol u + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

-   $\boldsymbol W \to$ matrix of markers recoded to numeric scale
-   $\boldsymbol u \to$ vector of marker effects 

. . .

::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
RR-BLUP assumes that all markers effects are normally distributed and have identical variance:

$$
\boldsymbol u \sim \mathcal N \left(\boldsymbol 0, \sigma^2_u \boldsymbol I \right)
$$

:::

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

$$
\boldsymbol u \sim \mathcal N \left(\boldsymbol 0, \sigma^2_u \boldsymbol I \right)
$$

```{r echo=FALSE}
ggplot() +
  stat_function(fun = function(x) dnorm(x, 0, 1), colour = '#b2bc63', 
                linewidth = 1.5) +
  theme_bw() + 
  xlim(-4,4) +
  theme_minimal()+
  theme(text = element_text(size = 18))
```

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

Solution via mixed model equation

$$
\begin{bmatrix}
\boldsymbol{1}^\prime \boldsymbol 1 & \boldsymbol 1^\prime \boldsymbol W \\
\boldsymbol W^\prime \boldsymbol 1 & \left(\boldsymbol W^\prime \boldsymbol W + \lambda \boldsymbol{I} \right)
\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}
\boldsymbol \mu \\
\boldsymbol u
\end{bmatrix} =
\begin{bmatrix}
\boldsymbol 1^\prime \boldsymbol y \\
\boldsymbol W^\prime \boldsymbol y
\end{bmatrix}
$$

. . .

**Shrinkage factor**: Shrinks the marker effects towards zero

$$
\lambda = \frac{\sigma^2_\varepsilon}{\sigma^2_u}
$$

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

Package `rrBLUP` [@endelman_ridge]

```{r echo=TRUE}
library(rrBLUP)
geno_rr = geno.code - 1  # Recoding the marker matrix
geno_rr[1:5,1:5]

mod = mixed.solve(y = dat$blue, Z = geno_rr) 
```

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}

```

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

$$
\hat{\boldsymbol g} = \boldsymbol W \hat{\boldsymbol u}
$$

```{r echo=TRUE}
GEBV = geno_rr %*% blup_rr
```

```{r echo=TRUE}

        text = element_text(size = 18))+

```

## Ridge Regression {.custom1}

**Model parameters**

$$
\hat{\sigma}^2_g = \sigma^2_u \times t
$$

```{r echo=TRUE}
Vg = mod$Vu * ncol(geno_rr); Vg
```


```{r echo=TRUE}
Ve = mod$Ve; Ve
mu = mod$beta; mu
geno_her = Vg/(Vg + Ve); geno_her
cor(dat$blue, GEBV, use = "complete.obs")
```

## BayesB {.custom1}

$$
\boldsymbol y = \boldsymbol 1 \mu + \boldsymbol W \boldsymbol u + \boldsymbol \varepsilon
$$

-   $\boldsymbol W \to$ matrix of markers recoded to numeric scale
-   $\boldsymbol u \to$ vector of marker effects 

. . .

::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
BayesB assumes that some markers are unimportant for the trait variation, hence have no effect. Furthermore, it relaxes the assumption that all markers have the same variance: 

$$
u_i \sim \mathcal N \left( 0, \sigma^2_{u_i} \right)
$$

:::

## BayesB {.custom1}

-   Prior for the variances: scaled inverse $\chi^2 \left[\sigma^2_{u_i} \sim \chi^{-2}\left(\nu\right)\right]$

. . .

-   Prior for the importance parameter (say, $I$): $I \sim \operatorname{Bernoulli}(\Pi)$

. . .

$$
\hat{g}_i = I_1 \times w_{1i} \times \hat u_1 + I_2 \times w_{2i} \times \hat u_2 + \dots + I_t \times w_{ti}  \times \hat u_t
$$

-   $I_j \to$ 1 or 0

## BayesB {.custom1}

Package `BGLR` [@perez_genome-wide_2014]

```{r echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
X_centred = scale(geno.code, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
ETA = list(list(X = X_centred, model = "BayesB")) ## This will determine the model
BayesB = BGLR(y = dat$blue, ETA = ETA, nIter = 70000, burnIn = 20000, 
              thin = 10, verbose = FALSE, saveAt = "complete_")
```

```{r echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE}
X_centred = scale(geno.code, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
ETA = list(list(X = X_centred, model = "BayesB")) ## This will determine the model
load(file = "../bayesbmod.RData")
```

. . .

::::: columns
::: {.column width="45%"}

::: {.callout-caution}
In [Bayesian models](https://github.com/storopoli/Estatistica-Bayesiana), you should mind the number of iterations, the burn-in phase and the thinning. The more, the better, but it will take longer for your model to run.
:::

## BayesB {.custom1}

**Convergence check through model diagnostics**: Package `coda` [@coda]

```{r echo=TRUE, fig.height=4}
library(coda)
varE = read.table("../complete_varE.dat")[,1]
varE_chain = mcmc(varE[2001:length(varE)]) # burnIn/thin + 1
plot(varE_chain)
```

## BayesB {.custom1}

**Effective sample size**: The number of independent samples from posterior distributions. The higher, the better. If low, increase `nIter` or `thin`

```{r echo=TRUE}
effectiveSize(varE_chain)
```

. . .

**Geweke convergence test**: evaluates if the MCMC chain reached a stationary state. It should be between -1.96 and 1.96. If not, increase `burnIn`

```{r echo=TRUE}
geweke.diag(varE_chain)
```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

**Define cross-validation parameters**

```{r echo=TRUE}
nfolds = 5
nrept = 5 
seed = 8  

cvdata = list() 
for (j in 1:nrept) {
  set.seed(seed*j) 
  cvdata[[j]] = dat[,c('gen', 'blue')]
  cvdata[[j]]$set = NA
  for (i in cvdata[[j]]$gen) {
    cvdata[[j]][cvdata[[j]]$gen == i,'set'] = sample(
      1:nfolds, 
      size = 1
    )
  }
}
```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Run RRBLUP in cross-validation

```{r echo=TRUE}
cv_rr = lapply(cvdata, function(x){
  res.list = list()
  for (i in unique(x$set)) {
    
    yNA = x$blue
    yNA[x$set == i] = NA
    
    mod_cv = mixed.solve(y = yNA, Z = geno_rr)
    
    pred = c(mod_cv$beta) + (geno_rr %*% mod_cv$u)
    
    res.list[[i]] = cbind(
      x[x$set == i,],
      yhat = pred[x$set == i,]
    )
  }
  res.list
})
cv_rr = lapply(cv_rr, function(x) do.call(rbind, x))
```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Run BayesB in cross-validation

```{r echo=TRUE, eval=FALSE}
cv_bb = lapply(cvdata, function(x){
  res.list = list()
  for (i in unique(x$set)) {
    
    yNA = x$blue
    yNA[x$set == i] = NA
    
    mod_cv = BGLR(y = yNA, ETA = ETA, nIter = 8000, burnIn = 1000, 
                  thin = 10, verbose = FALSE)
    unlink("*.dat")
    
    res.list[[i]] = data.frame(gen = x$gen, yhat = mod_cv$yHat) |> 
      left_join(x, by = "gen") |> filter(set == i)
  }
  res.list
})
cv_bb = lapply(cv_bb, function(x) do.call(rbind, x))
```


```{r echo=FALSE}
load(file = "../cv_bb.RDA")
```

## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Model evaluation

```{r echo=TRUE}
pa_rr = lapply(cv_rr, function(x) cor(x$blue, x$yhat, use = 'complete.obs'))
mspe_rr = lapply(cv_rr, function(x) sqrt(mean((x$blue - x$yhat)^2, na.rm = T)))

pa_bb = lapply(cv_bb, function(x) cor(x$blue, x$yhat, use = 'complete.obs'))
mspe_bb = lapply(cv_bb, function(x) sqrt(mean((x$blue - x$yhat)^2, na.rm = T)))
```


## Cross-validation {.custom1}

Model evaluation

```{r echo=TRUE}
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-height: 4.8

aux = data.frame(
  model = rep(c("RRBLUP", "BayesB"), each = nfolds*2),
  value = c(do.call(c, pa_rr), do.call(c, mspe_rr),
            do.call(c, pa_bb), do.call(c, mspe_bb)),
  param = c(rep(c("PA", "RMSPE"), each = 5), rep(c("PA", "RMSPE"), each = 5))
)

ggplot(data = aux, aes(x = model, y = value)) + 
  facet_wrap(~param, scales = "free_y") + 
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#b2bc63") + 
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 18))+
  labs(x = "Model") +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank())
```
